findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the runbook rotation step explicit that 'reload' means reconstructing the verifier — i.e. restart/replace the rebar-mcp process/container (the ADR blue-green swap), not merely rewriting the tokens file — because StaticTokenVerifier reads the file only at init.
evidence: _mcp_auth.py:207 `self._by_digest = _load_static_tokens(tokens_file)` invoked only in `__init__` — no per-request re-read
Plan: 'rotation is operator-driven (re-materialize + reload), which the runbook must state'
findings.finding: The `static` verifier loads its token set ONCE at __init__ (StaticTokenVerifier.__init__ → _load_static_tokens), so a rewritten tokens file is not observed by a running process. The plan's rotation model ('re-materialize + reload') is directionally consistent with this but does not state that 'reload' must reconstruct/restart the verifier process (or swap the MCP container per the ADR blue-green target); an operator who only re-materializes the file will see NO effect.
findings.location: Approach + rationale (rotation) / AC — runbook documents operator-driven rotation
scenarios: Operator rotates a PAT value in SSM, re-runs fetch-secrets.sh to rewrite the tokens file, but does not restart the rebar-mcp process → the old digest set stays live and the rotated token is rejected / the old token still accepted.

findings.finding: The materialization mechanism, as specified, writes the raw SSM PAT value into the on-box tokens file the `static` verifier reads, but that verifier's file format (src/rebar/_mcp_auth.py `_load_static_tokens`/`_parse_static_record`) REJECTS any plaintext `token` field and accepts only `token_sha256` (64-char hex digest) or `token_env` (env-var name). A file containing the raw PAT would raise AuthConfigError at boot, so the verifier oracle (accepts a materialized PAT) and the materialize oracle (file contains the SSM value) cannot both hold as written.
